subject: geography
title: UK Economic Change: Foundations 🌍

concepts.def: Extracting raw materials — farming, fishing, mining.
Manufacturing raw materials into goods — factories.
Decline of secondary manufacturing in a country.
Growing economic links between countries worldwide.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Every economy has four sectors:

1. Primary — farming, mining
2. Secondary — manufacturing
3. Tertiary — services
4. Quaternary — research/knowledge

As countries develop, employment shifts up the sectors.

After WWII the UK economy changed massively:

• Decline of coal, steel and shipbuilding
• Rise of services (finance, retail)
• Growth of quaternary (biotech, IT)

Today, ~80% work in services.

Causes of UK deindustrialisation:

• Globalisation — cheaper labour abroad
• Mechanisation — machines replaced workers
• Government policy in the 1980s
• Knowledge economy growth

The UK is now a post-industrial economy.
